# Review pack: review-testing

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-testing.<language>.md`. Where the instructions below say to load one of these files, use its section here instead; don't open the original. ## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Testing

Assesses the automated test suite: its shape (test pyramid), whether coverage is measured, whether tests can
actually fail, how test doubles are used, isolation and determinism, CI execution, coverage of production modules,
test-code quality, integration and contract tests, security-focused tests, and load/performance and resilience
tests.

#### Inputs

The capped, sampled list of test files, test configuration and CI test steps assigned by `compliance-inventory`,
plus the inventory's `testInventory` summary (test totals by category, production project roots and signals, when
present), and any authorization or integration-client file it lists for this subject. Review only those files.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/testing-rubric.md`: TSR-01…TSR-23, the signal table and thresholds. Always load.
- `references/standards/martinfowler-testing.md`: MFT-01…MFT-40. Always load.
- `references/standards/microsoft-unit-testing.md`: MSU-01…MSU-16 (language-neutral). Always load.
- `references/standards/security-testing.md`: STS-01…STS-14. Always load.
- `references/standards/azure-waf-testing.md`: AZT-01…AZT-09 (load and resilience tests). Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation, apply the closest element if it clearly fits. Otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md` and the five standards files.
2. Skip snapshot, recorded-cassette, fixture-data, generated and vendored files; note any skipped.
3. Classify tests as unit, integration or E2E/UI using the TSR-01 signal table. Names count only when the content
   agrees. Use the inventory's per-category totals for ratios; if only the sample is available, judge TST-01 only
   when the imbalance is unmistakable, with confidence `low`, and add
   `localized-standard-gap: pyramid judged from sample only` to `notes`. For an unknown test framework add
   `localized-standard-gap: unknown test framework <name>` once.
4. Evidence rule: a rubric threshold is a trigger, not a verdict. Fail only when the threshold is exceeded **and**
   reading the tests confirms the problem. State the counted value in the evidence excerpt; confidence `medium`
   unless the value is at least twice the threshold.
5. If the repository has no automated tests: fail TST-01, TST-02, TST-06 and TST-07; mark TST-03, TST-04, TST-05,
   TST-08 and TST-09 N/A ("no tests"); evaluate TST-10 … TST-13 if they apply.
6. For each check TST-01…TST-13, evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when" condition holds; if none
   apply, mark the check N/A with that reason. TST-09 needs integration points (a data store, an outbound HTTP or
   messaging client, or ≥ 2 services), TST-10 access control (N/A for libraries and CLIs without it), and TST-11
   untrusted-input parsing. TST-07 needs production roots; without them judge it only from test-project names that
   obviously mirror production projects, with confidence `low`. TST-02 never fails on a coverage percentage: record
   TSR-05 observations in `notes` only. TST-04 never fails for a mocking style or library, only for the
   TSR-08/TSR-09 signals.
   TST-12 (load tests) applies to a deployable service with request or message endpoints; it is N/A for libraries,
   CLIs and static front ends. Load-test signals: `*.k6.js`/k6 scripts (`import http from 'k6/http'`), `*.jmx`,
   `locustfile.py`, Gatling simulations, NBomber projects, Artillery YAML, hosted load-test configs; use
   `testInventory.signals.loadTests` when the sample has none. No load tests at all fails AZT-01 (confidence
   `medium`); AZT-02 … AZT-05 are judged only when load tests exist. Never fail for a missing stated target: without
   one, AZT-02 passes when any threshold is set.
   TST-13 (resilience tests) applies when the code makes remote calls (`testInventory.signals.integrationPoints`).
   Resilience signals: tests that make a fake, mock server or HTTP fault handler return errors, delays or timeouts and
   assert retry, breaker or fallback behaviour (WireMock/MockServer fault responses, `HttpMessageHandler` stubs,
   Polly/Resilience4j test setups, `responses`/`respx` errors), Toxiproxy config, Chaos Mesh/Litmus manifests, hosted
   chaos experiments; use `testInventory.signals.faultInjection` when the sample has none. Fail AZT-06/AZT-07 only
   when retry, timeout or breaker logic is visible in the files and no test exercises its failure path. AZT-09 is
   judged only when fault-injection or chaos definitions exist; their absence alone is never a failure.
7. Boundaries: don't fail for whether CI builds every change (review-software-lifecycle SL-01), SAST or analyzer
   gating (SL-11), branch protection (SL-04), README test instructions (review-maintainability MAINT-01),
   production-code design or testability smells (review-software-quality), production-code correctness of
   authorization, input handling, errors or logging (security skills), API contract documentation
   (review-api-design), restore tests or DR drills (review-disaster-recovery), alert testing (review-monitoring),
   or test-only packages in production scope (review-dependency-management). Load, performance, resilience and
   chaos tests are judged here (TST-12/TST-13; decision D-3, 2026-11-09); the code's own retry, timeout and breaker
   logic is review-reliability's, and its performance is review-performance's.
8. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md`;
   `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
9. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `TSR-01`); the report script derives `standard` and `url`
   from it, so don't write them.
10. Note strengths where the suite is clearly well shaped, coverage is published, tests are deterministic and
    readable, contract tests guard service boundaries, authorization has thorough negative tests, or load and
    fault-injection tests gate the pipeline.

#### Output

Labels: don't write `subject` or `subSubject`; the report script takes them from `references/checklist.md`
(the `Subject:` line and the check's `Sub-subject` column). Follow `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/standards/testing-rubric.md`

*Load rule: TSR-01…TSR-23, the signal table and thresholds. Always load.*

### Compliance Reviewer Testing Rubric — local standard

- Level: informational only; severity always comes from the owning check (SKILL.md).
- **Thresholds are triggers, not verdicts.** Fail only when the threshold is exceeded **and** reading the tests
  confirms the problem (e.g. a 50-line test that builds one large expected object is not a long test). Counts are
  reading estimates: state the counted value in the evidence excerpt and use confidence `medium` unless the value is
  at least twice the threshold. An approved analyzer output (step `02`) may support a count but is never required.
- **Counting.** Ratios (TSR-02) use the inventory's `testInventory.totals` when present; otherwise `totalMatched` with
  folder or project names; from the 12-file sample only when the imbalance is unmistakable (confidence `low`, plus
  `localized-standard-gap: pyramid judged from sample only` in `notes`).

#### Signals (part of TSR-01)

Folder and project names (`*.UnitTests`, `*.IntegrationTests`, `e2e/`, `tests/integration/`) count only when the
content agrees. Unit = no infrastructure (no database, network, filesystem, container, browser or in-process web host).
Integration = a real or containerized dependency, or an in-process host. E2E/UI = a deployed or full-stack target.

| Signal | .NET | Java | Python | JS/TS | Go |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Test framework | xUnit, NUnit, MSTest | JUnit 5, TestNG | pytest, unittest | Jest, Vitest, Mocha | `testing` |
| Assertion | `Assert.*`, FluentAssertions `.Should()`, Shouldly | `assert*`, AssertJ `assertThat` | `assert`, `self.assert*`, `pytest.raises` | `expect(...)`, `assert` | `t.Error*`, `t.Fatal*`, testify |
| Expected-exception test (counts as an assertion) | `Assert.Throws*`, `.Should().Throw` | `assertThrows` | `pytest.raises`, `assertRaises` | `toThrow`, `rejects` | error checks |
| Skip | `[Fact(Skip=…)]`, `[Ignore]`, `[Explicit]` | `@Disabled`, `@Ignore` | `@pytest.mark.skip`, `xfail`, `@unittest.skip` | `it.skip`, `xit`, `test.todo` | `t.Skip` |
| Order dependence | `[Order]`, `TestCaseOrderer`, `[Priority]` | `@TestMethodOrder`, `@Order`, `dependsOnMethods` | `pytest-order`, `pytest-dependency` | `--runInBand` used to hide shared state | — |
| Integration | Testcontainers, `WebApplicationFactory`, `TestServer` | Testcontainers, `@SpringBootTest`, `@DataJpaTest` | Testcontainers, DB fixtures, `TestClient` against a real app | Testcontainers, supertest against a real DB | `httptest` + real DB |
| HTTP fakes | WireMock.Net | WireMock, MockServer | `responses`, `respx`, `pytest-httpserver` | `nock`, `msw` | `httptest.Server` |
| Contract tests | PactNet | Pact JVM, Spring Cloud Contract | pact-python | pact-js | pact-go |
| E2E/UI | Playwright, Selenium | Selenium, Playwright, REST-assured (base URL) | Playwright, Selenium | Playwright, Cypress, Puppeteer | chromedp |
| Coverage | coverlet, `--collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"`, dotCover | JaCoCo | coverage.py, pytest-cov | c8, nyc/istanbul, `--coverage` | `-cover`, `-coverprofile` |
| Fuzz / property-based | SharpFuzz, FsCheck, CsCheck | Jazzer, jqwik | Hypothesis, atheris | fast-check, jsfuzz | `func FuzzXxx` |
| DAST | OWASP ZAP baseline/API scan job, Nuclei, Burp CI | (same) | (same) | (same) | (same) |
| Report published | Codecov or Coveralls upload, a coverage artifact, a PR coverage comment, a `reportgenerator` step, a documented local command |  |  |  |  |

An unknown test framework: classify by content where possible and add
`localized-standard-gap: unknown test framework <name>` to `notes` once.

**Excluded files:** snapshot files (`*.snap`, `__snapshots__/`, `*.verified.*`), recorded HTTP cassettes, test-data
fixtures, `obj/`, `target/`, `build/`, `node_modules/`, `vendor/`. Note and skip them if handed over.

#### Thresholds

| Measure | Threshold | Element |
|---|---|---|
| Pyramid shape | E2E/UI tests ≥ unit tests, **or** unit tests < 50 % of classified tests | TSR-02 |
| Assertion-free tests | ≥ 2 sampled tests **or** > 10 % of sampled test methods | TSR-06 |
| Test doubles per unit test | > 5 | TSR-08 |
| Skipped tests | any skip without a reason or tracking reference, **or** > 5 % of sampled tests skipped | TSR-12 |
| Test length | > 40 logical lines | TSR-16 |
| Copied arrange block | > 10 lines repeated in ≥ 3 tests | TSR-17 |

#### Elements

| ID | Criterion (fail when …) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| TSR-01 | *(Classification.)* Tests are classified unit, integration or E2E/UI by the signals above. Names count only when the content agrees, and unclassifiable tests are left out of ratios. Not failed on its own. | any tests | TST-01 |
| TSR-02 | The pyramid is inverted per the thresholds, counted from inventory totals, or from the sample only when unmistakable (confidence `low`). | ≥ 2 test levels or E2E present | TST-01 |
| TSR-03 | Logic-bearing production code is tested only through integration or E2E tests: there is no unit-test project, folder or file. | any tests | TST-01 |
| TSR-04 | No coverage collection is configured anywhere (test project, build file, CI step or documented command) per the signals, or coverage is collected but never published or reported. | any tests | TST-02 |
| TSR-05 | *(Observation; never fails.)* An enforced threshold below 50 %, or a hard gate at ≥ 95 %, is recorded in `notes` as `TST-02 observation: …`. | coverage threshold configured | TST-02 |
| TSR-06 | Assertion-free tests reach the threshold: no assertion, verification or expected-exception check. A "smoke" test that only proves construction or startup counts unless it is named and documented as a smoke test. | any tests | TST-03 |
| TSR-07 | Assertions are tautological or too weak to fail for a real defect: `Assert.True(true)`, asserting a stub returns what it was set up to return, or only not-null or "no exception" where a concrete value can be checked. | any tests | TST-03 |
| TSR-08 | Over-mocking: more than 5 doubles in one unit test, the class under test is itself mocked or partially mocked, or value objects, DTOs or collections are mocked. | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| TSR-09 | Assertions only verify mock calls that restate the implementation (every call, strict order and arguments) where an observable result or state exists. | mocks with verification | TST-04 |
| TSR-10 | Order dependence or shared state: ordering attributes used to make tests pass (signals), mutable `static` or module-level state shared between tests, or a shared database with no reset, rollback or fresh container. | any tests | TST-05 |
| TSR-11 | Timing and non-determinism: sleeps used as waits (`Thread.Sleep`, `Task.Delay`, `time.sleep`, `setTimeout`) with no polling or timeout, unseeded randomness, or the current time read directly (`DateTime.Now`, `Instant.now()`, `datetime.now()`, `Date.now()`) in tests or in tested code with no seam. | any tests | TST-05 |
| TSR-12 | Skipped tests reach the threshold. A skip with a reason *and* a tracking reference is a quarantined test and passes, unless it exceeds the share. | any tests | TST-05 |
| TSR-13 | CI config in the repository has no step that runs the test suite on push to the default branch **and** on pull requests (`dotnet test`, `mvn verify`, `gradle test`, `pytest`, `npm test`, `go test`, or a script that calls them). | always | TST-06 |
| TSR-14 | Test failures don't fail the pipeline: `continue-on-error: true` or `allow_failure: true` on the test job, `\|\| true`, `testFailureIgnore`, `-DskipTests`/`maven.test.skip`, or `--passWithNoTests` while tests exist. | CI config present | TST-06 |
| TSR-15 | A logic-bearing production project or package has no corresponding tests (no `X.Tests`, no `tests/x`, no test source set, and no tests elsewhere that reference it). Exempt: contracts or DTO-only projects, composition roots and hosts, generated code, and migrations. | production roots known (`testInventory.productionRoots`) | TST-07 |
| TSR-16 | A test method exceeds 40 logical lines, or contains control flow (`if`, loops, `switch`, `try/catch` other than for an expected-exception assertion), confirmed by reading. | any tests | TST-08 |
| TSR-17 | Complex arrangement is copied instead of shared: an arrange block of > 10 lines repeated in ≥ 3 tests, with no builder, factory or helper. | any tests | TST-08 |
| TSR-18 | A data store or outbound HTTP or messaging client exists, but no integration test exercises it: no repository test against a real engine (container or local) and no client test against a fake server. An in-memory provider alone doesn't count. | integration points exist | TST-09 |
| TSR-19 | ≥ 2 services in the repository communicate over HTTP or messaging, or the code calls a separately deployed in-house service, and there are no contract tests or provider verification (Pact, Spring Cloud Contract, schema-based verification). | ≥ 2 services, or a client of an in-house service | TST-09 |
| TSR-20 | Tests call production or shared external endpoints (hard-coded production URLs or connection strings, real cloud resources) instead of local or containerized dependencies. | any tests | TST-09 |
| TSR-21 | No negative authorization tests: nothing asserts that an unauthenticated request is rejected (401) or that the wrong role or owner is refused (403/404), and custom authorization handlers or policies have no tests. | access control present | TST-10 |
| TSR-22 | Security-relevant error paths are untested: no test checks that invalid input is rejected or that an exception becomes a generic error response without internal details. | HTTP endpoints or input validation present | TST-10 |
| TSR-23 | Parsers, deserializers or validators of untrusted input have no fuzz or property-based tests (signals), **and** no DAST job runs in the pipeline. Either one passes the element. | untrusted input parsed | TST-11 |

## File: `references/standards/martinfowler-testing.md`

*Load rule: MFT-01…MFT-40. Always load.*

### Martin Fowler (martinfowler.com) — testing, localized summary

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| MFT-01 | Tests are automated so the software can be released at any time. Regression checking doesn't depend on manual click-through. | always | TST-06 |
| MFT-02 | The suite is shaped like a pyramid: many small, fast unit tests, fewer coarser tests, and very few end-to-end tests (no "ice-cream cone"). | any tests | TST-01 |
| MFT-03 | Unit tests make up the largest share and stay fast, so they don't touch databases, the filesystem or the network. | any tests | TST-01 |
| MFT-04 | Collaborators are replaced with doubles only when the real ones are slow or awkward. Otherwise real (sociable) collaborators are fine. | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| MFT-05 | Test doubles replace external or slow parts. Mocks and stubs are distinguished, and the terms aren't used interchangeably. | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| MFT-06 | Private methods aren't tested directly (no reflection or visibility hacks). Wanting to test one signals a class that should be split. | any tests | TST-03 |
| MFT-07 | Tests exercise the public interface and observable behavior, including non-trivial and edge paths, not implementation details or trivial accessors. | any tests | TST-03 |
| MFT-08 | Each test has a clear arrange/act/assert (given/when/then) structure. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MFT-09 | Every point where data is serialized or deserialized (database, REST, queue, files) has an integration test. One integration point is tested at a time, against dependencies run locally, never against production. | integration points exist | TST-09 |
| MFT-10 | At least one repository or data-access integration test runs against a real engine. In-memory substitutes can behave differently from production. | data store used | TST-09 |
| MFT-11 | Separate services and third-party APIs are replaced by fake servers in integration tests, and those fakes are verified by contract tests. | outbound HTTP or messaging client | TST-09 |
| MFT-12 | Interfaces between separately deployed consumers and providers are covered by consumer-driven contract tests that the provider verifies in its pipeline. | ≥ 2 services, or a client of an in-house service | TST-09 |
| MFT-13 | End-to-end tests cover only the most valuable user journeys. API-level end-to-end tests are preferred over browser tests where they give the same confidence. | E2E tests exist | TST-01 |
| MFT-14 | UI behavior (including APIs and CLIs as user interfaces) is tested with framework-level tools where possible, not only through full-stack browser tests. | UI or CLI present | TST-01 |
| MFT-15 | Features are verified from the user's perspective by acceptance tests, which may be written at a lower level than the UI. | always | TST-07 |
| MFT-16 | Pipeline stages are ordered by speed and scope. Fast tests run first, and narrow integration tests may run alongside unit tests. | CI config present | TST-06 |
| MFT-17 | Tests are pushed as low in the pyramid as possible. A higher-level test that only duplicates lower-level coverage is removed. | ≥ 2 test levels | TST-01 |
| MFT-18 | Test code gets the same care as production code. Each test checks one condition, and readability is preferred over DRY. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MFT-19 | Coverage is measured to find untested code. The coverage tool is run regularly and its gaps are reviewed. | always | TST-02 |
| MFT-20 | Coverage isn't treated as a quality target. A mandated percentage invites gaming, up to and including assertion-free tests. | coverage threshold configured | TST-02 |
| MFT-21 | Coverage figures are interpreted, not mandated: well below half signals trouble, near 100 % is suspicious, and upper 80s–90s is typical of thoughtful testing. | coverage threshold configured | TST-02 |
| MFT-22 | When simple production changes need long test changes, the cause is usually duplication in the tests. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MFT-23 | Non-deterministic (flaky) tests are fixed or quarantined promptly. Quarantine is limited in size and age and kept out of the main pipeline. | any tests | TST-05 |
| MFT-24 | Tests are isolated and pass in any order. Each test builds its start state from scratch (or rolls back a transaction) instead of relying on earlier tests. | any tests | TST-05 |
| MFT-25 | Shared state in statics, singletons and context (for example the logged-in user) doesn't leak between tests, and tear-down failures are loud. | any tests | TST-05 |
| MFT-26 | Asynchronous results are awaited with callbacks or short polling under a timeout, never with bare sleeps. A timeout fails with a clear message. | async code under test | TST-05 |
| MFT-27 | Logic is moved out of asynchronous plumbing (Humble Object) so it can be tested synchronously. | async code under test | TST-05 |
| MFT-28 | Functional tests don't depend on live remote systems. They use doubles for determinism. | remote dependencies | TST-05 |
| MFT-29 | The system clock is wrapped so tests can control time. Clock stubs are re-initialized per test, and direct clock calls can be blocked by a build check. | time-dependent code | TST-05 |
| MFT-30 | Leaks and hidden randomness are exposed: pooled resources are sized to 1 in tests and randomizers are stubbed to fixed values. | pooled resources or randomness | TST-05 |
| MFT-31 | Test doubles are named for their role (dummy, fake, stub, spy, mock) so a reader knows what is being verified. | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| MFT-32 | State verification with real objects is used where collaboration is easy. Doubles and behavior verification are used where collaboration is awkward or state can't reveal the outcome (for example caching). | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| MFT-33 | Interaction-verifying tests couple to the implementation and hinder refactoring. Strict call and argument matching is used only where the interaction *is* the behavior. | mocks with verification | TST-04 |
| MFT-34 | Whatever the unit-test style, the suite also has coarser acceptance or system tests across the system. | any tests | TST-01 |
| MFT-35 | The build is self-testing. A comprehensive suite runs in the build, and any failing test fails the build. | CI config present | TST-06 |
| MFT-36 | A change isn't complete until automated tests verify its new behavior. | always | TST-07 |
| MFT-37 | Every push to mainline triggers a build that runs the tests. | CI config present | TST-06 |
| MFT-38 | The commit build stays fast (about ten minutes). Slower tests move to later pipeline stages, independent tests run in parallel, and a bug caught late gets a commit-stage test. | CI config present | TST-06 |
| MFT-39 | Tests that need infrastructure run against a production-like environment (same versions, typically containers), not hand-maintained shared servers. | integration tests exist | TST-09 |
| MFT-40 | Contract tests against external services run on an automated schedule. | contract tests or fakes of external services | TST-09 |

## File: `references/standards/microsoft-unit-testing.md`

*Load rule: MSU-01…MSU-16 (language-neutral). Always load.*

### Microsoft .NET unit testing best practices — localized summary

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.
- **Applies to every language.** The page targets .NET, but the localized rules (naming, arrange/act/assert, no logic,
  one act, seams) are language-neutral. xUnit- and MSTest-specific notes are not localized.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSU-01 | Unit tests are fast (milliseconds each), so the whole unit suite can run on every change. | unit tests | TST-01 |
| MSU-02 | Unit tests are isolated: they have no dependency on outside factors such as the file system or a database. | unit tests | TST-05 |
| MSU-03 | Unit tests are repeatable: the same code gives the same result on every run. | unit tests | TST-05 |
| MSU-04 | Tests are self-checking. Pass or fail is decided automatically, with no human inspection of output. | any tests | TST-03 |
| MSU-05 | A coverage percentage doesn't measure quality, and overly ambitious coverage goals are counterproductive. | coverage threshold configured | TST-02 |
| MSU-06 | Fake, stub and mock are used correctly. A mock is asserted against and a stub isn't, and names say which is which. | unit tests with doubles | TST-04 |
| MSU-07 | Unit tests have no infrastructure dependencies. Unit and integration tests live in separate projects or folders, so the unit project doesn't reference infrastructure packages. | unit tests | TST-01 |
| MSU-08 | Test names state the unit under test, the scenario and the expected behavior, using one consistent convention. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-09 | Arrange, act and assert are visibly separated, and assertions aren't mixed into the act step. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-10 | Test inputs are the simplest values that verify the behavior, with no extra properties or arbitrary values. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-11 | No unexplained "magic" literals. Meaningful values are named constants. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-12 | Test bodies contain no logic (`if`, loops, `switch`, string building). Parameterized tests are used instead. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-13 | Test-specific setup is visible in the test or a helper, and isn't hidden in a shared setup/teardown that tests don't all need. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-14 | Each test has a single act step. Multiple cases use separate or parameterized tests. | any tests | TST-08 |
| MSU-15 | Private behavior is verified through the public method that uses it. | any tests | TST-03 |
| MSU-16 | Static dependencies such as the current time are reached through a seam (an interface or provider) so tests control them. | time or static dependencies | TST-05 |

## File: `references/standards/security-testing.md`

*Load rule: STS-01…STS-14. Always load.*

### Security testing sources — localized summary (testing sentences only)

- Level: informational only; severity is the owning check's default.
- Scope: only the sentences about *testing*. The rest of these pages is owned by the security skills and
  `review-software-lifecycle`.

| ID | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| STS-01 | Authorization logic has automated unit and integration tests, covering deny-by-default, safe failure when a check fails, and attribute or relationship policies. | access control present | TST-10 |
| STS-02 | Tests confirm that the designed permissions (least privilege) are actually enforced. | access control present | TST-10 |
| STS-03 | The handling of exceptions and authorization failures is verified by tests. | access control present | TST-10 |
| STS-04 | Logging is part of testing: it works as specified, events are classified consistently, and the logging mechanism resists injection. | security event logging present | TST-10 |
| STS-05 | The application's behavior when logging fails (no space, lost connectivity, no write permission, logger errors) is tested. | security event logging present | TST-10 |
| STS-06 | Functional access control is included in unit and integration tests. | access control present | TST-10 |
| STS-07 | Injection flaws are detected by automated testing that includes fuzzing of inputs (parameters, headers, URL, cookies, JSON/XML). | untrusted input parsed | TST-11 |
| STS-08 | (PW.8.1) Which kinds of executable-code testing are used is a deliberate, documented choice, for vulnerabilities not found by review or static analysis. | untrusted input parsed | TST-11 |
| STS-09 | (PW.8.2 ex. 1) Security features (authentication, authorization, validation, cryptographic use) have robust functional tests. | security features present | TST-10 |
| STS-10 | (PW.8.2 ex. 2) Dynamic vulnerability testing is integrated into the automated test suite. | HTTP endpoints present | TST-11 |
| STS-11 | (PW.8.2 ex. 3) Previously reported vulnerabilities have regression tests so they aren't reintroduced. | a fixed vulnerability is referenced (advisory, changelog, test name) | TST-10 |
| STS-12 | (PW.8.2 ex. 5) Fuzz-testing tools are used to find input-handling issues. | untrusted input parsed | TST-11 |
| STS-13 | The project fuzzes: OSS-Fuzz or ClusterFuzzLite integration, or fuzz or property-based test functions in a supported language. | untrusted input parsed | TST-11 |
| STS-14 | Checked-in scripts run all of the repository's tests, and a CI platform runs them on every pull request. | CI config present | TST-06 |

## File: `references/standards/azure-waf-testing.md`

*Load rule: AZT-01…AZT-09 (load and resilience tests). Always load.*

### Azure Well-Architected and Architecture Center testing guidance — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the pages use no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.
- Scope: generic. Azure product names in the sources (Azure Load Testing, Chaos Studio) are generalized ("load-test
  tool", "fault-injection tool"). Tool names a reviewer can look for are in `../SKILL.md` step 6.

#### TST-12 — Load and performance tests

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZT-01 | REVIEW | Automated load tests exist for the service's critical flows, scripted as synthetic transactions with realistic data and usage patterns; load testing comes first, stress, spike and soak tests as risk grows. | deployable service with request or message endpoints | TST-12 |
| AZT-02 | REVIEW | Load tests have acceptance criteria with explicit pass/fail thresholds per metric (for example p95 latency, error rate, throughput), derived from the stated performance targets. | load tests exist | TST-12 |
| AZT-03 | REVIEW | Performance tests run in the deployment pipeline or on a recorded automated schedule, so regressions and drift are caught before production. | load tests exist | TST-12 |
| AZT-04 | REVIEW | Load tests target a production-like environment (matching compute, autoscaling and caching settings, or a deliberately scaled-down copy for non-critical workloads), never a developer machine as the only target. | load-test config names a target environment | TST-12 |
| AZT-05 | REVIEW | Results are compared with a recorded baseline (stored results, baseline file or run comparison), so regressions are visible. | load tests run in CI or on a schedule | TST-12 |

#### TST-13 — Resilience tests

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AZT-06 | REVIEW | Transient-fault handling is tested: retry policies, timeouts and circuit-breaker thresholds are exercised under failure, including exhaustion (all retries fail, breaker open) and the switch to fallback or degradation. | code makes remote calls with retry, timeout or breaker logic | TST-13 |
| AZT-07 | REVIEW | Retry behaviour is tested deterministically: a mock or fake returns the range of errors the retry strategy detects, or an HTTP fault library in automated tests changes status codes, headers or latency. | code makes remote calls with retry logic | TST-13 |
| AZT-08 | REVIEW | Critical dependency failures are tested: each fallback activates, partial failures (added latency, intermittent errors) are covered, and one failing dependency doesn't break unrelated functionality. | code calls remote dependencies on critical flows | TST-13 |
| AZT-09 | REVIEW | Fault-injection or chaos experiments have a stated hypothesis and a contained blast radius, start in non-production environments, run on a regular cadence or in the pipeline, and may be combined with load tests. | fault-injection or chaos definitions in scope | TST-13 |
